layers.note: A tree of seasonally flooded bottomlands, swamps and stream sides.

moisture.note: Wet ground that floods in winter.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 600 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −2 °C, gone by −6 °C, up to about 13 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −20 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −28 °C.

warmest_c.note: Warm, dry summers: warmest-month means from about 15.5 to 27 °C, gone below 13 °C and above 30.5 °C.

degree_days_0.note: A long warm season: about 3,100 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 2,400.

degree_days_5.note: About 1,600 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 1,100: it stays in warm lowlands and on the lower slopes.

moisture_index.note: It grows where the ground stays wet whatever the climate's moisture index, so only the driest climates (below about 0.1) rule it out; the site's own moisture places it.

summer_rain.note: A Mediterranean-type climate: its range lies where at most about 0.2 of the year's precipitation falls in summer, gone by 0.35.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Oregon ash grows on bottomlands and by streams from Puget Sound to central California (Silvics of North America, vol. 2). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
